Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the thoughtful discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned before we book the sizing session: 

Recap (what I heard)
- Primary workload: real-time ledger enrichment + multi-turn summarization on transaction batches.
- Target throughput: ~450 reqs/sec at peak (95th percentile burst pattern across US traffic).
- Latency SLO: 95th p99 <= 250ms for generation-only calls; batch/async paths can be higher.
- Model preference: open-model base (Llama2-70B-class) with KV-cache and quantization.
- Data posture: sensitive PII; prefer Dedicated (isolated pool) + customer-managed KMS.

What we want from the Dedicated sizing call
- Align on peak per-second token throughput and sequence lengths.
- Confirm target latency SLOs and what we can trade (batching vs. endpoint latency).
- Validate KV cache requirements and expected cache hit patterns.
- Walk through autoscale/burst policy and failover plan.

Proposed next step: 60–75 minute Dedicated Capacity Sizing call (technical deep-dive). I can lead the infra/runbook side; Karthik will cover kernel/serving choices.

Proposed slots (PT):
- Thu Jun 10: 10:00–11:15 PT
- Thu Jun 10: 13:00–14:15 PT
- Fri Jun 11: 09:30–10:45 PT

If none of these work, please suggest two times that fit your calendar and we’ll lock something. I attached a short capacity_estimate_template.xlsx to help you drop in sample traffic numbers before the call — filling that out (even roughly) will shorten the meeting.

Attaching: capacity_estimate_template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Thanks — looking forward to continuing.

—

I can take the kernel/quantization section and will include a short slide set. Preliminary notes: 
- 8-bit (QLoRA / int8) usually maintains quality for embedding/generation tradeoffs and gives 1.8–2x throughput vs fp16 on our throughput profiles.
- 4-bit/4-bit+ tricks (gptq-style) give more density but expect ~10–20% added latency variance on tail unless we adjust kernel tiling.
- For Ledgerly's p99 target (<=250ms) we should plan for a mixed strategy: lower-latency endpoints on fp16/8-bit for real-time path and a batched quantized path for bulk enrichment.

I'll attach a short preliminary runbook (prelim-throughput-runbook.pdf) with expected GPU counts for the sample traffic Jordan will drop in the spreadsheet.

Agenda looks good. I can be on the call Thu Jun 10 13:00 PT. Marcus, can you confirm the autoscale numbers?
